task_text: IKEA MuJoCo GLADOM tray table (IKEA GLADOM tray table (AA-1832218-3), full seven-operation scope) with two 7-DoF Franka Panda arms, each with the MuJoCo Menagerie Panda hand (two-finger, tendon-coupled). Build the GLADOM tray table: cross frame B into frame A, drive the long screw and the bottom screw, place the ring and drive its two screws, and set the tray on the ring. Success requirements: The retention joints of frame B, the ring and the four screws are all latched. Every part except frame A is at its assembled pose relative to frame A: gap within 0.8 mm along frame A's z axis, lateral within 1 mm, tilt within 2 degrees (screws: axis tilt; frame B and the ring may be rotated 180 degrees, the tray 7.5 degrees), relative speed below 0.025 m/s. The two ring screws may use either ring receiver, but distinct ones. The tray is free (never jointed) and supported by the ring (contact above 0.01 N in at least 12 of 36 samples over the last 0.15 s, and above 0.01 N on average over them); no robot contact with any furniture part. All of the above hold continuously for 0.15 s. The benchmark's terminal rules, the same in every IKEA MuJoCo task, come on top of these requirements. When your rows end: (1) the requirements above hold; (2) the parts are released: no robot link touches any part; (3) every part is at rest: at most 0.01 m/s and 0.05 rad/s; (4) the simulation never broke down: no non-finite state, no MuJoCo BADQACC / BADQPOS / BADQVEL warning, no contact of a part deeper than 10 mm, at any time. The grader then holds your last row for 1.0 s more and requires (1)-(4) again at its end. Mechanism: Screw threads and frame A's four nut sleeves are SDF meshes (0.5 mm pitch, right-hand): a screw advances only by being turned. Retention welds to frame A switch on when the scene's acceptance gates hold. The tray is never jointed.
